label: early original-phase input of p, or of a k/1/u/n/q/f/z token after an earlier one from that set
explanation: Fires almost only while the original tokens are being read (97% of mass), at early positions t=1..4 (peaks at t=2-3, weak at t=0, rare after t=5), and depends on the input token. p is by far the strongest trigger (42% of p inputs active, 37% of mass), followed by k, 1, u, n, q, f, z. The other tokens in this set fire mostly when an earlier set token has already been seen. Activations reach their largest values when set tokens are adjacent (n n p, n 1 p, n f p); p at t=2 after two set tokens is the maximum. It is weaker on later repeats of a token (in_first=0 holds 13% of mass). It is near-silent at <DEL> and through the copy phase, and does not fire on other letters (b, m, s are weak). The predicate captures about 81% of mass at about 0.72 precision. The residue is context-dependent: some set tokens with an earlier set token stay silent, and some activations at t=5 are missed.
